 Hyundai Department Store and Kolmar Korea Showcase Flagship Products at Korean Wave Expo in Australia
 Sim Useop 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.08 15:46 
 View 
 View Count 
 Enlarge image 
 ▲ The booth view of Hyundai Department Store and Mediquitous at the 2026 Melbourne Korean Wave Expo 
 Hyundai Department Store and Kolmar Korea participated in the 2026 Melbourne Korean Wave Expo held at the Melbourne Showgrounds, introducing beauty and fashion brands and products to local consumers and buyers. 
 Hyundai Department Store announced that it operated a promotional pavilion measuring 96 square meters, the largest among participating companies, alongside Mediquitous, a partner in supporting K-brand overseas expansion. 
 The promotional pavilion featured flagship products from a total of 13 brands, including domestic skincare brands such as Wellage and The Yoo, as well as K-fashion brands like Rolarola, Mahagrid, Stand Oil, and Double Lovers. 
 Products featuring Hyundai Department Store's proprietary character "Heendy" and items from the IP platform "WithMUU," which distributes K-pop artist merchandise, were also introduced. 
 Kolmar Korea also participated in the expo alongside six client companies, conducting export consultations valued at approximately 6.8 billion won. 
 From November 5 to 7, Kolmar Korea operated its booth at the expo in collaboration with Goodai Global (Round Lab), Parket (Mixsoon), Mercico (Hubblem), Iunik (Iunik), Gibest (Nine Tales), and HK inno.N (B-ownd). 
 A total of about 150 export consultations were conducted on-site, accounting for more than 10 percent of all consultations at the expo, Kolmar Korea explained. 
 The two-day event targeted at general consumers drew about 30,000 visitors, with an estimated 15,000 of them visiting the Kolmar Korea booth. 
 At the event venue, Kolmar Korea displayed products such as sunscreen, essence, cream, and sheet masks, while operating programs where visitors could check UV protection effects and test five different sun care products. 
 According to KOTRA, last year's imports of South Korean skincare products by Australia reached 147.7 million dollars, representing a 42.1 percent increase from the previous year. 
 (Photo provided by Hyundai Department Store, Yonhap News)
